stats.fact: DeepSeek Harness official GitHub repo has 212,253 stars and 24,916 forks as of 2026-09-05
DeepSeek Harness is MIT-licensed, written in TypeScript, and built on the Cordis plugin kernel (arXiv paper 2608.25512)
Quick start is 'npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web', which starts the Web UI at http://127.0.0.1:3080 by default
A plugin is a TypeScript module exporting an 'apply' function; the framework calls apply with a ctx context to register capabilities
dsh ships five profiles: web, headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, and acp; 'dsh --profile headless "job"' runs one fresh persisted session and exits
The agent loop itself is a plugin; every part of the product (model adapter, tool registry, session log) is replaceable from configuration
Schedule overlay supports reminders via schedule_create, schedule_list, schedule_delete with after_seconds, at, or every_seconds (min 300s) targets
Three-role capability design separates Service Definition, Service Provider, and Consumer so providers can be swapped via cordis.yml without touching the tool

angles: Everything-is-a-plugin: the agent loop, model adapter, tools, and session log are all replaceable plugins — no privileged core to patch
Agent lifecycle: turn/step lifecycle with durable replay on session/event and live control on agent/* events
Runbooks via headless mode: dsh --profile headless 'job' runs one-shot persisted sessions for automation and CI
Scheduling: session-local reminders with schedule_create/list/delete for recurring agent tasks
Plugin development walkthrough: first plugin, building a tool with defineTool, config, and publishing
Three-role capability design for building replaceable, independently-evolving capabilities
Profiles and bundles: web, headless, sdk, acp — how to compose and patch the plugin tree
Developer-preview caveats: compatibility-breaking changes mean pinning versions and reviewing SAFETY.md
